page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, providing a 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. It runs on x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor featuring 1 physical core with 2 threads via multithreading. The CPU provides a dedicated allocation with 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Supported hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. The instance does not include local disk storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on remote block storage and standard cloud networking.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a stress-ng score of 2669.58 and average single-threaded compression throughput. However, due to its physical configuration of 1 core split across 2 vCPUs, overall multi-core throughput is limited, yielding lower scores in multi-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate weak uncached read and write performance, measuring 26.64 GB/sec and 20.4 GB/sec respectively. Database operations, Redis throughput, and static web serving tests reflect resource constraints typical of small dual-vCPU configurations.

The n2d-standard-2 instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight compute scenarios where single-threaded speed is preferred over large parallel capacity. By utilizing AMD EPYC processors with dedicated vCPUs, it avoids CPU credit throttling found in burstable instance classes while maintaining a small resource footprint. This configuration is suitable for lightweight microservices, development environments, background job processing, and low-traffic backend applications.

It is suitable for lightweight microservices, development environments, simple background jobs, and low-traffic web applications.
